parsed.attack: Most journeyman and apprentice licensing exams are open-book with the code book on the desk, so drilling conduit and box fill table values into memory trains a skill the exam does not test; the felt pain apprentices actually describe is not knowing where to look fast enough, which is answered by tabbing a code book and by Ugly's Electrical References at $14, already in nearly every apprentice's truck. This audience does spend on exam prep, which cuts both ways - Mike Holt, Tom Henry and the union hall's own course already own that spend and carry the instructor endorsement the referral loop is banking on, so the behaviour to change is not 'start buying prep' but 'switch from the thing your instructor named to an unbranded app'. The demand evidence given is three failed consumer habit apps, i.e. negative evidence about the category, with the acuteness of a booked exam date asserted rather than observed for this particular wedge.
parsed.strongest_defence: Open-book does not mean no preparation - the exams are severely time-constrained and candidates fail on speed, which is exactly what spaced repetition of the tables you keep getting wrong fixes - and the proof of demand is that this trade already spends $50-300 per candidate on prep against a licence worth tens of thousands a year in earnings, so willingness to pay $29 is demonstrated rather than hoped for.
parsed.verdict_reason: The audience's willingness to pay at this moment is genuinely demonstrated, but the specific wedge drills recall for an exam that permits lookup, so it may be selling against a pain this cohort does not feel.
